task_3.title: Expire JWTs exactly at the exp boundary
task_3.description: PyJWT 2.6.0 fixes expiration handling so tokens become invalid at the exact configured expiration time instead of remaining usable through the matching second. This closes a boundary-condition bug and makes expiration checks align with the documented meaning of the exp claim, including when leeway is applied.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that JWT expiration enforcement invalidates a token at the exact moment its effective expiration time is reached, so a token is no longer accepted when the current time equals its exp value after accounting for leeway.

expectation.grounded: When PyJWT validates the exp claim during token decoding, a token whose exp is equal to the current validation time boundary must be treated as expired. The same rule must apply when leeway is provided, using the adjusted boundary. Decoding such a token should raise ExpiredSignatureError rather than succeed for one additional second.
expectation.conceptual: JWTs should stop being accepted exactly when they expire, not after an extra boundary second. If expiration leeway is configured, that grace period should shift the cutoff, but the token should still become invalid immediately once the adjusted cutoff is reached.

constraints.grounded: Do not change exp claim validation outside the equality boundary fix. Tokens with exp strictly later than the effective current-time threshold must remain valid, tokens with exp earlier than or equal to that threshold must be expired, and existing ExpiredSignatureError signaling for expired tokens must remain the observable failure mode.
constraints.conceptual: Preserve normal JWT expiration behavior and only correct the exact cutoff edge case. Valid future-dated tokens should continue to decode normally, while tokens at or past the expiration cutoff should be rejected consistently.

behavior: A token is considered expired when its exp claim is exactly equal to the current validation time.
A token is considered expired when its exp claim is earlier than the current validation time.
If leeway is configured, expiration is evaluated against the current time minus the leeway window, and equality with that adjusted cutoff is also expired.
Decoding a token at the expiration boundary raises ExpiredSignatureError instead of returning a decoded payload.
acceptance_criteria: When a token is decoded at the exact second represented by its exp claim, it should be rejected as expired.
When a token is decoded before its exp cutoff, it should continue to decode successfully.
When leeway is supplied and the token's exp equals the adjusted cutoff time, it should be rejected as expired.
When a token is expired by the boundary rule, the observable failure should be ExpiredSignatureError.

task_4.title: Correct the mislabeled 2.5.0 release heading
task_4.description: Version 2.6.0 is a documentation-only release that corrects a typo in the published heading for version 2.5.0. No code, API surface, or runtime behavior changes are evidenced by the provided diff.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that the 2.6.0 update corrects the mislabeled 2.5.0 release heading so users reading release information are not misled about the affected version, while preserving all existing library behavior.

expectation.grounded: The published release information for 2.6.0 should correct the version 2.5.0 heading typo referenced in the release note. No public API names, callable behavior, return values, warning behavior, or error behavior should change, because the provided code diff contains no runtime modifications.
expectation.conceptual: The upgrade should only improve release-note accuracy. Users should not need to change application code or expect any difference in how the library behaves at runtime.

constraints.grounded: Do not introduce changes to the library's public API, runtime semantics, exception behavior, or configuration behavior. The update must remain limited to correcting release documentation/version labeling, consistent with the absence of code changes in the provided diff.
constraints.conceptual: This release must be non-functional: it should fix release metadata or documentation wording only, without altering observable library behavior.

behavior: The version 2.5.0 heading referenced by the 2.6.0 release materials is corrected to the proper version label.
No observable runtime behavior changes are introduced in the library.
No user migration steps, compatibility changes, or API updates are required for this release.
acceptance_criteria: When a user reads the 2.6.0 release information, it should correctly identify the referenced 2.5.0 heading without version-label ambiguity.
When upgrading from 2.5.0 to 2.6.0, applications should behave the same as before with no changes to public API usage.
The release should not introduce new runtime warnings, errors, or feature behavior changes.

task_2.title: Remove cryptography stub package from crypto extra
task_2.description: The 2.6.0 update removes the `types-cryptography` typing stub from the library's `crypto` optional dependency set because it is not required to use cryptography-backed features and may be inaccurate for newer cryptography versions. The upgrade should preserve crypto functionality while simplifying installation of the optional crypto support.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that upgrading to 2.6.0 no longer requires the `types-cryptography` stub package when users install the library with crypto support enabled, while keeping cryptography-backed JWT functionality available through the existing optional crypto dependency.

expectation.grounded: Installing version 2.6.0 with the `crypto` extra should no longer pull in or require `types-cryptography`. The `crypto` extra should continue to represent runtime crypto support for the library's public cryptography-backed features without depending on a separate typing-stub package.
expectation.conceptual: Users who opt into crypto support should get the runtime dependencies needed for those features, but they should not receive an unnecessary type-stub dependency. The upgrade should behave like a packaging cleanup rather than a feature removal.

constraints.grounded: Do not make `types-cryptography` a required dependency of the `crypto` extra in 2.6.0. Preserve the meaning of the `crypto` extra as the opt-in path for cryptography-backed functionality, and avoid changing observable runtime behavior solely because the stub package was removed.
constraints.conceptual: The change should only reduce unnecessary installation baggage. It should not break existing crypto-enabled usage or force users to install typing-related packages to keep normal runtime behavior.

behavior: The optional `crypto` installation path no longer includes the `types-cryptography` package.
Users can continue using cryptography-backed library capabilities without installing a separate typing stub.
Dependency resolution for the `crypto` extra is simplified to runtime-relevant packages rather than type-checking aids.
acceptance_criteria: When a user installs version 2.6.0 with the `crypto` extra, the resolved optional dependencies should not include `types-cryptography`.
When a user upgrades from 2.5.0 to 2.6.0 for crypto-enabled usage, they should not need to add or retain `types-cryptography` to keep normal runtime crypto functionality working.
When users rely on the library's crypto-backed features at runtime, the upgrade should not change those features' availability merely because the typing stub was removed.

task_1.title: Raise the minimum supported cryptography version to 3.4.0
task_1.description: Version 2.6.0 raises the minimum supported `cryptography` dependency to 3.4.0. This updates the library's supported environment baseline without introducing an evidenced public API or runtime behavior change in the library code itself.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that version 2.6.0 only supports environments using `cryptography` 3.4.0 or newer, so installations and supported usage align with the updated dependency baseline.

expectation.grounded: The library's 2.6.0 release must require `cryptography>=3.4.0` as the supported dependency floor. Based on the provided materials, no additional public API additions, removals, or runtime behavior changes are evidenced beyond this dependency-version requirement.
expectation.conceptual: Upgrading to 2.6.0 should mean the library now expects a newer `cryptography` version. Users on supported dependency versions should see unchanged library behavior, while older dependency baselines are no longer part of the supported upgrade path.

constraints.grounded: Do not introduce unrelated changes to JWT encoding, decoding, algorithm handling, exceptions, or other public behaviors unless they are required by the dependency floor update. For environments already using `cryptography` 3.4.0 or newer, the upgrade should preserve existing observable library behavior.
constraints.conceptual: The upgrade should only change dependency compatibility expectations, not alter how existing features behave for users already on a supported stack.

behavior: The minimum supported `cryptography` version is raised to 3.4.0 in version 2.6.0.
Environments pinned below `cryptography` 3.4.0 are outside the supported dependency range for this release.
No direct runtime or public API behavior change is evidenced in the provided library code diff beyond the dependency support baseline change.
acceptance_criteria: When a user upgrades to library version 2.6.0, the documented and supported dependency baseline should require `cryptography` 3.4.0 or newer.

When the library is used in an environment that already has `cryptography` 3.4.0 or newer, upgrading to 2.6.0 should not introduce any additional observable API or behavior change beyond the dependency update.
When a user relies on an older `cryptography` version than 3.4.0, that environment should no longer be treated as supported for version 2.6.0.

task_5.title: Reject JWTs with future issued-at timestamps
task_5.description: The 2.6.0 update closes a validation gap in JWT decoding by treating an issued-at claim in the future as a not-yet-valid token. Tokens whose `iat` exceeds the current time beyond the allowed leeway are now rejected instead of being accepted, improving time-based token validity checks without changing the existing malformed-`iat` error behavior.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that JWT decoding rejects tokens whose `iat` claim is set in the future beyond the allowed leeway, so tokens cannot be treated as valid before their effective issued-at time while preserving existing handling for malformed `iat` values.

expectation.grounded: When decoding a JWT that includes an `iat` claim, the library should treat `iat` values greater than the current decode time plus configured leeway as not yet valid and raise `ImmatureSignatureError`. Existing `iat` type validation must remain in place so non-integer `iat` values still raise `InvalidIssuedAtError`.
expectation.conceptual: Issued-at should participate in token freshness checks the same way other time-based validity claims do. A token with an issued-at time too far in the future must be rejected as premature, while malformed issued-at values should continue to surface as invalid input.

constraints.grounded: Do not regress the current contract for malformed `iat` claims: values that are not interpretable as integers must still fail with `InvalidIssuedAtError`. Do not reject a token for immaturity based on `iat` when the claim is at or before the current time plus leeway. The future-time comparison must honor decode-time leeway.
constraints.conceptual: Keep backward-compatible behavior for bad `iat` formats, and only add rejection for tokens that are observably ahead of the allowed clock-skew window. Tokens that are already within the permitted validity window should not start failing solely because they contain `iat`.

behavior: JWT decode now fails with `ImmatureSignatureError` when an `iat` claim is later than the current time plus leeway.
The future-`iat` validation uses the same leeway tolerance applied to other time-based validity checks, allowing limited clock skew.
An `iat` claim that cannot be interpreted as an integer continues to fail with `InvalidIssuedAtError`.
A token whose `iat` is current, in the past, or within the allowed leeway is not rejected by this new immaturity check.
acceptance_criteria: When decoding a token whose `iat` is later than the current time and still later than the current time plus configured leeway, decoding should raise `ImmatureSignatureError`.
When decoding a token whose `iat` is in the future but falls within the configured leeway window, it should not be rejected for immaturity on the basis of `iat` alone.
When decoding a token whose `iat` is current or in the past, it should not be rejected for immaturity on the basis of `iat` alone.
When decoding a token whose `iat` value is not interpretable as an integer, decoding should raise `InvalidIssuedAtError`.
